question: Should OpenClaw adopt gateway-local multi-user identity, authorization, and exact-resource plugin contracts as a permanent core capability for Teams-style sharing?
rationale: The branch changes the gateway trust model, shared database, public protocol, plugin SDK, agent delegation, and Control UI boundary; implementation quality alone cannot decide whether this belongs in core or who will own its long-term security and compatibility.

options.title: Sponsor a gated stack
options.body: Approve the direction but require a clean, independently reviewable stack plus explicit security ownership, upgrade proof, and real-system evidence before landing.

options.title: Accept this integrated PR
options.body: Treat the feature as an exceptional cohesive change and review the rebased monolith after complete security, migration, and live-behavior proof is supplied.

options.title: Keep core single-operator
options.body: Decline the new core trust model and pursue external collaboration only after identifying the smallest generic plugin APIs needed outside core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a gated stack
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but require a clean, independently reviewable stack plus explicit security ownership, upgrade proof, and real-system evidence before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Teams proposal directly extends the Workspaces architecture they introduced and merged, making them the best available owner for the product-boundary decision.
